lessons.title: Variables, Data Types & Arrays
body: Declare data with const (fixed) and let (changeable). Avoid var in modern code.
Core types: number, string, boolean, null, undefined, object, array. Check with typeof.
Arrays are the analyst's weapon: map for transforming, filter for selecting, reduce for aggregating.
Example: const clean = data.filter((x) => x.value != null).map((x) => x.value);

quiz.q: Which array method is right for summing all values?
quiz.explain: reduce folds an array into a single value — ideal for aggregations like totals and averages.

quiz.q: What does typeof null return in JavaScript?
quiz.explain: typeof null returns 'object' — a historic JS quirk every analyst must memorize.

lessons.title: Lab: Total Sales Function
body: Write function solve(input) that takes an array of numbers and returns their total.
Ignore non-number values (null, undefined, string).
Example: solve([10, null, 20]) returns 30.

lessons.title: CV Structure HR Reads in 30 Seconds
body: One page for fresh graduates: name, contact, headline, education, experience, skills.
Write numbers, not traits: “managed Rp5M/day cash with zero variance” beats “hard worker”.
Use a recent formal photo and a professional email (your name, not a nickname).

quiz.q: How many pages should a fresh graduate CV be?
quiz.explain: HR scans dozens of CVs — one dense page beats three watery ones.

quiz.q: Which experience bullet is strongest?
options: Managed Rp5M/day cash for 6 months with zero variance
quiz.explain: Numbers + duration + verifiable results. Traits without proof get skipped.

lessons.title: Portfolio superbright.id/u/you
body: HR almost always clicks the portfolio link — minimum: 1 project, 1 certificate, skill list.
Tell each project with Problem → Action → Result.
Update your profile every finished path, not once a year.

quiz.q: Most convincing project-story formula?
quiz.explain: Problem gives context, action shows skill, result proves impact.

quiz.q: Minimum viable public profile?
quiz.explain: HR needs proof of work in 1 minute: project, certificate, skills.

lessons.title: Answer “Tell Me About Yourself” in 2 Minutes
body: Use Now → Background → Proof → Target: who you are, background, one proof, why this role.
Don't read your CV — HR already read it. Add what's not written.
Drill with a timer until it's exactly 2 minutes, no more no less.

quiz.q: Right order for “tell me about yourself”?
quiz.explain: Open with your present, close with why you want this role.

quiz.q: Ideal self-intro length?
quiz.explain: Two minutes fits 4 points without boring HR.

lessons.title: First Salary & Trick Questions
body: Research market salaries from similar listings in your city before naming a number.
Answer with a range (“7–9 million, open to discussion”), not a fixed number.
For “what's your weakness?”: name one real weakness + how you handle it.

quiz.q: Best way to answer salary expectations?
options: Give a range based on market research
quiz.explain: A range shows you researched the market but stay flexible.

quiz.q: Best answer to “what's your weakness?”
options: Real weakness + how you handle it
quiz.explain: HR judges honesty and growth mindset, not perfection.

lessons.title: Where Are Your Customers?
body: Indonesian SME customers live on Shopee, TikTok, and WhatsApp — pick ONE channel first.
Real photos of your goods beat stock photos: buyers judge honesty.
Consistency beats viral: 1 post/day for 30 days beats one hit post.

quiz.q: First marketing step for a tiny SME team?
options: Open accounts on every platform at once
Wait until you have a content team
quiz.explain: One living channel beats five dead ones.

quiz.q: Most trusted SME content?
options: Real photos and videos of the goods
quiz.explain: Buyers judge honesty: real products, real process, real owner.

lessons.title: First Rp50K Ad
body: One ad, one goal: incoming WhatsApp chats — not likes, not follows.
Target your city radius first, not all of Indonesia.
Track cost per chat. An ad losing money 3 days straight: kill it, swap the photo.

quiz.q: Success metric for a first SME ad?
quiz.explain: Chats = buyers. Likes don't pay the shop rent.

quiz.q: When to kill a losing ad?
quiz.explain: Three days is enough to judge one creative on a small budget.

keuangan-gaji-bulanan.title: Manage Your Monthly Salary Without Leaks

lessons.title: The 50-30-20 Rule, Boarding-House Edition
body: 50% needs (rent, food, transport), 30% wants, 20% savings — adapt, don't memorize.
Pay yourself first: autodebit savings on payday, not from month-end leftovers.
Emergency fund target: 3x monthly spending, kept apart from daily account.

quiz.q: Best time to save from salary?
quiz.explain: Month-end leftovers are almost always zero. Autodebit forces you to pay your future first.

quiz.q: Healthy emergency fund target?
quiz.explain: Three months gives breathing room during layoffs or illness without debt.

lessons.title: Beware of Illegal Lenders & Scams
body: Legal lenders are OJK-registered — check the list before borrowing, not the ads.
Never give your OTP to anyone, including callers claiming to be bank or police.
Received a suspicious transfer? Don't forward it — verify the VA and report, don't panic.

quiz.q: Before borrowing from a lender, you must check what?
quiz.explain: Illegal lenders collect through terror. The OJK legality list is the first filter.

quiz.q: A caller claims to be your bank and asks for your OTP. Right response?
options: Refuse and hang up, then call the official bank
Give it, they know your data
Ask them to wait while you transfer first
quiz.explain: Banks never ask for OTPs. Verify through official bank channels.

lessons.title: Hierarchy & Talking to Your Boss
body: Report before being asked: a short update every afternoon beats a panic report every crisis.
Got an impossible task? Answer “yes, so which deadline is the top priority?” — not silence.
Deliver criticism privately + bring solutions; praise openly.

quiz.q: Boss gives a task impossible to finish today. Best response?
options: Accept, then ask priorities and a realistic deadline
Stay silent and overtime without word
quiz.explain: Bosses need information to reprioritize — give data, not drama.

quiz.q: Where to criticize a coworker?
quiz.explain: Private criticism saves face; solutions show you want to help.

lessons.title: Meetings & Feedback
body: Arrive 5 minutes early with notes and one question — that's half your meeting grade.
Take feedback with: listen → ask for examples → make an improvement plan.
Generations differ: seniors value process, juniors value speed — adapt your language.

quiz.q: Best meeting prep in a boss's eyes?
options: Arrive early with notes and a question
Arrive on time with no prep
quiz.explain: Good questions show you read the material and thought.

quiz.q: Receiving harsh-but-fair feedback. Right response?
options: Listen, ask for concrete examples, make a plan
quiz.explain: Concrete examples turn emotion into fixable data.
